title: Optical-disc stamper family tree for DRAM array nanoimprint
idea: Adapt CD/DVD/Blu-ray replication: one e-beam-written quartz master is electroformed into nickel 'father', 'mother' and 'son' stampers (each generation multiplies copies ~10x), and the sons serve as UV-nanoimprint working templates for the periodic array layers (capacitor holes, landing pads, bitlines). Each son is retired after a fixed imprint count, as disc plants do, so defects never accumulate; EUV is kept only for the periphery.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): replaces 3-4 of the 5-7 EUV array exposures with NIL tools at ~1/5 the cost and ~1/10 the power of an EUV scanner; claim 15-25% wafer-cost cut. Risks: overlay at 12 nm-class pitch and imprint defectivity.

title: Hard-disk patterned-media trick: copolymer density multiplication for templates
idea: Copy the HDD bit-patterned-media playbook: e-beam writes only a sparse guide lattice at 2-3x the final pitch, a PS-b-PMMA or high-chi block copolymer fills in the hexagonal lattice by directed self-assembly, and the rectified pattern is etched into the NIL or mask master.
why: Template and mask mastering cost (fact 4): e-beam write time falls by the square of the multiplication factor (4-9x), so template refresh is cheap; the native hexagonal lattice matches the honeycomb 6F2 capacitor layout.

title: Holographic-grating interference lithography for the periodic cell lattice
idea: Adapt diffraction-grating and security-hologram production: print the strictly periodic array layers with three-beam 193 nm interference or displacement Talbot lithography (one periodic phase mask scanned in z), which writes hexagonal hole lattices across a full field with near-unlimited depth of focus and no projection lens; a cheap KrF trim exposure clears the array edges.
why: EUV dependence and scanner capex (fact 4): interference tools cost ~$5-15M versus $200M+ for EUV, need no product reticle, and with one spacer pitch split reach array pitch; claim ~3 EUV layers removed.

title: Pharmaceutical isolators: a ballroom-free DRAM fab
idea: Pharma replaced Grade-A cleanroom suites with sealed isolators; keep ISO-1 air only inside FOUPs, EFEMs and tool minienvironments, run the building at ISO-8, and give every tool maintenance access through pharma-style rapid-transfer ports (alpha/beta double doors) so the tool interior is never exposed to room air.
why: Fab capital, energy and build time: cleanroom shell plus HVAC is ~15-25% of fab construction cost; claim 10-15% capex and 20-30% facility-energy reduction and a faster build.

title: Shipyard block construction: prefabricated fab modules built in parallel
idea: Shipyards build fully outfitted hull blocks in parallel halls and join them at the dock; build a DRAM fab as ~300 factory-made blocks (subfab utility skids, pre-piped tool pads, ceiling cassettes with fan filters, abatement modules) made off-site in a U.S. yard while foundations are poured, then craned in and bolted together.
why: Time-to-capacity and capital (fact 4): build time 3-5 years toward ~18-24 months, cutting capitalized interest; repeated block designs give a learning curve across multiple U.S. fabs.

title: Steel mini-mill disruption: EUV-free DUV mini-fabs for mature DRAM
idea: Nucor beat integrated mills by entering at rebar with cheap electric-arc mini-mills; build 10-20k wafer-starts/month fabs using refurbished 193i scanners and SAQP to make 1y/1z-class DDR4, LPDDR4 and CXL-expander dies, sell into the commodity tier the HBM-focused majors are abandoning, then climb node by node.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: ~$3-5B per mini-fab versus $15B+; zero EUV; DUV tools are available on the secondary market; adds supply in under 3 years.

title: Solar porous-silicon lift-off: reusable seed wafers for DRAM substrates
idea: Adapt the PV kerfless process: anodize a porous-silicon double layer on a reusable 300 mm CZ seed, grow a 10-20 um device-grade epitaxial Si film, bond it to a cheap handle (reclaimed or multicrystalline Si), and cleave along the porous layer; the seed is re-polished and reused 20-50 times.
why: Scarce resources (high-purity quartz crucibles, polysilicon, CZ pullers): prime CZ silicon per wafer drops ~20x. Risk: epi defect density versus the retention tail.

title: Aircraft-leasing model for scanners and etchers
idea: Copy AerCap/GECAS: a lessor buys scanners, etchers and deposition tools in bulk, leases them to fabs on 5-8 year operating leases with standard return conditions and maintenance reserves, and re-markets returned tools to the next fab, including startups and mini-fabs.
why: Capital intensity (depreciation ~55% of wafer cost): turns capex into opex, lowers the entry barrier for new U.S. entrants, and bulk purchasing plus secondary-market liquidity lowers lease rates.

title: Solar project finance: offtake-backed DRAM fab special-purpose vehicles
idea: Finance each fab like a utility-scale solar farm: a special-purpose vehicle owns the fab, hyperscalers sign 10-year take-or-pay bit offtake contracts at indexed prices (like PPAs), and the transferable advanced-manufacturing investment credit is sold to tax-equity buyers, so the fab borrows non-recourse debt at infrastructure rates.
why: Cost of capital: WACC from ~10-12% to ~6-7% cuts the capital charge in wafer cost by ~25-30%; offtake removes the boom-bust risk that stops fabs from being built.

title: Pure-play foundry model with an open DRAM cell PDK
idea: Borrow TSMC's split of design from manufacturing: a DRAM foundry runs one qualified cell process with an open process design kit (cell, sense amp and redundancy libraries), and many fabless memory designers tape out custom DRAMs (AI-tuned page sizes, CXL, in-memory compute) on shared capacity.
why: Capital utilization and innovation: pooled demand keeps the fab full across cycles, and new memory products need design budgets (~$20-50M) instead of a $15B fab.

title: Bottling-line linear fab: single-wafer flow without FOUP queues
idea: Borrow the beverage bottling line: arrange process modules along a linear inert-gas track balanced to one takt time, so each wafer flows step to step singly with no FOUP batching, stockers or overhead hoists; slow modules are duplicated in parallel lanes as in line balancing.
why: Throughput and working capital: cycle time ~60-90 days toward ~10-15 days, WIP inventory down ~5x, AMHS/stocker capex removed, faster yield learning; claim 10-20% capital-productivity gain.

title: PCB laser direct imaging: maskless DUV for low-volume periphery layers
idea: PCB makers dropped phototools for DMD laser direct imaging; apply a 193/248 nm micromirror-array maskless writer to DRAM's relaxed periphery layers (40 nm and up) and HBM base-die redistribution layers, so custom memory variants need no new reticle set.
why: Mask capital and agility: a DRAM mask set costs $10-30M+; custom low-volume AI memory becomes nearly mask-free; the throughput penalty is tolerable on a few layers.

title: MicroLED mass transfer: printing known-good DRAM array tiles
idea: Borrow microLED micro-transfer printing: build ~200 um DRAM array tiles on a donor wafer, test them, then elastomer-stamp only known-good tiles onto periphery wafers at the sense-amp interface; failed sites are re-printed as microLED repair does.
why: Yield and capital: die yield becomes tile yield (~99%+), letting new fabs run aggressive cells profitably at low yield, shrinking redundancy and fuse area, and letting several small fabs feed one assembler.

title: Accumulative roll bonding: 3D DRAM tiers from repeated layer transfer
idea: Metallurgy builds nanolaminates by repeatedly rolling and folding; build 3D DRAM tiers by hydrogen-implant smart-cut transfer of 30-50 nm single-crystal Si sheets onto an oxide-bonded stack, then bond stack to stack to double tiers each round (8 to 16 to 32 to 64), instead of growing a 100+ layer Si/SiGe superlattice.
why: No manufacturable 3D cell (fact 2): avoids the strain-relaxation limit on epi stack height, gives monocrystalline channels in every tier, and reaches 64 tiers in ~6 bond rounds.

title: Self-stratifying paint: one-coat multilayer litho stacks
idea: Industrial coatings use self-stratifying paints that separate into primer and topcoat in one application; formulate a single spin-on film that, during bake, segregates by surface energy into a silicon-rich hardmask bottom layer, an organic underlayer and a fluorinated-segment resist top layer.
why: Process steps and track capex (fact 4): saves ~2 coats and bakes per patterned layer across ~40 litho layers, ~5-8% fewer total steps and less chemical use.

title: Decaffeination supercritical CO2: collapse-free drying for taller capacitors
idea: Adapt coffee decaffeination and supercritical extraction plants: after the wet etch that frees capacitor pillars, replace IPA drying with supercritical CO2 exchange (zero surface tension) so capillary forces never bend or stick pillars, letting aspect ratio climb toward 100-115:1 with fewer support layers.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) via yield: removes pattern collapse as the AR limit; claim +20-40% Cs headroom and fewer support-mesh deposition and etch steps.

title: Food-packaging spatial ALD: conveyor-speed liners and spacers
idea: Roll-to-roll barrier-film lines for food packaging coat by moving the substrate under fixed precursor and purge zones; use atmospheric spatial ALD heads for DRAM's low-aspect-ratio ALD films (spacers, liners, periphery gate stacks) and reserve slow temporal ALD only for the deep capacitor stack.
why: Tool capex (fact 4): spatial ALD runs 5-10x more wafers/hour on thin conformal films; claim ~30% fewer ALD chambers per fab.

title: Single-use bioreactor logic: disposable etch-chamber liner cartridges
idea: Biopharma moved from cleaned stainless tanks to single-use bags; give high-AR etch and CVD chambers robot-swappable disposable liner cartridges (yttria-coated alumina shells) replacing 12-24 h wet-clean maintenance.
why: Capital productivity: etch tools are the largest tool count after litho; a 5-10% uptime gain avoids hundreds of millions in tools per fab and stabilizes chamber seasoning.

title: Continuous-recharge Czochralski from PV: many ingots per crucible
idea: PV pullers grow 5-10 ingots per crucible by recharging granular polysilicon through a feed tube; adapt multi-recharge Cz, with devitrification-promoting crucible coatings for longer life, to 300 mm DRAM-grade wafers with in-line oxygen control.
why: High-purity quartz chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%): crucible use per wafer down 3-5x and puller utilization up ~30%.

title: Army-arsenal GOCO model for a strategic U.S. DRAM fab
idea: Like the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant, the government owns the fab building and tool set and a commercial memory maker operates it under a cost-plus-fee contract, selling output commercially with a guaranteed defense allocation.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. share (1-2%): removes the private-capital hurdle and cycle risk for the first domestic high-volume fab; public cost of capital ~4% versus ~10% private.

title: Airport baggage CT: inline X-ray laminography for 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Adapt CT and laminography from airport scanners and BGA inspection into an inline compact-source X-ray laminography tool that reconstructs tier-by-tier recess depth, channel thickness and capacitor fill in 100-tier 3D DRAM stacks on every lot without cross-sectioning.
why: 3D DRAM manufacturability (fact 2) and ramp speed: replaces slow destructive TEM; cutting ramp by months is worth ~$1B on a $15B fab.

title: Egg-grading economics: retention-graded dies sold with refresh maps
idea: Food grading sells every egg by grade; test each DRAM die's retention tail and sell weaker dies as a managed-refresh grade with a per-die weak-row map stored on the module, so the controller refreshes only those rows faster instead of the die being repaired or scrapped.
why: Effective fab output: recovers ~5-10% of dies lost to retention fails or repair limits and needs fewer redundant rows and fuses (fact 7); each yield point is ~1% cost per bit.

title: SpaceX rideshare: multi-project shuttle wafers on a DRAM pilot line
idea: Like rideshare launches that carry dozens of satellites, a national DRAM pilot line offers quarterly multi-project shuttle runs: startups and universities buy part of a wafer on a standard access-transistor and periphery flow and drop in their own capacitor or cell module.
why: Capital barrier to new cells: a cell experiment falls from $100M+ for a private line to ~$0.1-1M per shuttle slot, filling the U.S. pipeline of DRAM-class cells.

title: Aerospace anodizing: aluminum-oxide nanopore templates for capacitors
idea: Instead of EUV plus deep plasma etch of 60-75:1 holes, deposit thick aluminum, nanoimprint shallow seed pits, and anodize it in oxalic or sulfuric acid (aircraft anodizing chemistry) so ordered vertical pores grow 1-3 um deep, then line them with TiN/ZrO2-Al2O3/TiN. Elements: Al, O, S, C, Ti, Zr, N only.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and etch capex (fact 4): AR ~115 is trivial for anodization; a ~$1M wet bath replaces $5-10M high-AR etchers; no W or Ru.

title: Optical-fiber stack-and-draw: sliced silicon-core fiber capacitor plates
idea: Draw a preform of doped-silicon rods in silica (molten-core fiber method), restack and redraw until cores are ~20-30 nm at cell pitch, fuse the bundle into a boule, slice it like an ingot into wafers of vertical Si electrodes in SiO2, recess the silica to expose 1-3 um Si pillars as bottom electrodes, and bond onto the transistor wafer through oversized landing pads that absorb lattice misregistration. Elements: Si, O, B, P.
why: Removes deep etch and EUV for the capacitor layer (facts 1, 4): aspect ratio set by slice thickness, not etch; fiber draw is cheap, continuous and U.S.-strong.

title: MLCC base-metal-electrode chemistry: nickel and acceptor-doped titanate capacitors
idea: The MLCC industry replaced Pd with Ni electrodes by firing BaTiO3 in reducing gas with Mn/Mg acceptor doping and a reoxidation anneal; apply the recipe to DRAM: Ni or TiN electrodes with Mg/Mn-doped SrTiO3 or CaTiO3 (thin-film k ~100-200), crystallized at low oxygen pressure and then reoxidized, with no Ru electrode and no Hf.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): meets the k ~70+ target, so AR can drop from ~70 to ~30-40, halving etch time and collapse risk; Sr, Ca, Ti, Mg, Mn, Ni, O are abundant.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor forming: anodically grown TiO2 dielectric that self-heals
idea: Electrolytic capacitors anodize ('form') their dielectric at a set voltage and 're-form' to heal weak spots; deposit a Ti/Al storage electrode, turn on every wordline so each cell is biased through its own access transistor, and anodize the electrode surface in a borate electrolyte to a voltage-set TiO2 thickness (~2 nm/V), re-forming after the crystallization anneal.
why: Hf/Ru-free dielectric without ALD (facts 1, 4): thickness is set by voltage, not precursor diffusion, so it is conformal at any AR; a wet bench costs ~10x less per pass than ALD; TiO2 k ~40-90.

title: Metallized-film capacitor self-clearing: aluminum plates that isolate shorts
idea: Film capacitors survive breakdowns because their thin Al electrode vaporizes around a fault; make the DRAM cell plate a thin Al-Ti film and apply a wafer-level clearing pulse, so a plate-to-node pinhole short burns open locally and becomes one dead cell (handled by ECC) instead of a shorted plate that kills a whole mat or chip.
why: Yield, redundancy and periphery (fact 7): lets dielectrics thin for more Cs without mat-level yield loss and cuts repair rows; Al replaces W/TiN plate fills.

title: In-situ leach mining: copper-catalyzed wet etching of deep holes
idea: As in-situ leaching dissolves ore where it lies, use metal-assisted chemical etching: copper catalyst dots (instead of Au/Ag) defined by imprint or self-assembly on silicon sink vertically in HF/H2O2, digging capacitor holes or vertical channels beyond 100:1 at room temperature in a wet bench.
why: Deep-etch capex and EUV (facts 1, 4): ~10x cheaper tools, unlimited AR, no plasma damage, no W-doped or thick carbon hardmask. Risks: catalyst wander and Cu contamination control.

title: Carbon-fiber furnaces: iron-catalyzed nanotube forests as capacitor cores
idea: Adapt carbon-fiber and nanotube-forest CVD: place Fe catalyst dots on Al2O3 at each storage-node pad, grow vertical multiwall carbon nanotubes 1-2 um tall at ~450-550 C, then ALD-wrap them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each tube is the scaffold and conductor of a tall capacitor that is grown rather than etched.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and etch capex (fact 4): AR >100 comes free with growth, removing the mold, hardmask and deep-etch module; Fe, C, Al, Ti, Zr, N only.

title: Squeeze casting: high-pressure forced aluminum fill replacing tungsten plugs
idea: Die casting pushes molten metal into fine cavities with pressure; replace CVD tungsten contacts and landing pads with PVD aluminum forced into TiN-lined openings by a 60-100 MPa argon anneal at 400-450 C, run in batch hot-isostatic-press chambers adapted from aerospace castings.
why: W-free metallization (constraint) and RC: removes WF6 CVD and W targets; Al ~3 uOhm-cm versus 10-20 for narrow W lowers contact resistance and allows smaller contacts; batch HIP is cheap per wafer.

title: Case hardening: fully silicided poly buried wordlines without tungsten
idea: Steel case hardening converts a surface in place by diffusion rather than depositing a coating; fill buried-wordline trenches void-free with doped poly-Si, then convert the upper part fully to NiSi or C54 TiSi2 by metal deposition and anneal, keeping a thin poly region near the drain for low GIDL.
why: W-free (constraint) with fewer steps (fact 4): poly fills sub-10 nm trenches without seams, needs no WF6 or nucleation barrier, and silicide reaches ~15 uOhm-cm, competitive with scaled W.

title: Titanium-industry cold crucibles: quartz-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Titanium and multicrystalline-silicon casting melt the charge inside water-cooled segmented copper 'cold crucibles' where induction fields hold the melt off the wall; adapt a cold-crucible induction Czochralski puller to 300 mm DRAM ingots, metering oxygen through a controlled SiO feed to keep the interstitial oxygen needed for gettering.
why: High-purity quartz chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%): eliminates quartz crucibles entirely with only Cu and Si, and lowers crucible-dissolution contamination.

title: Fiber-optic soot deposition: fully synthetic silica crucibles
idea: The fiber industry makes 9N silica by flame hydrolysis of SiCl4 (VAD/OVD soot) on a mandrel; deposit soot on a crucible-shaped mandrel and sinter it into a fully synthetic crucible with a crystallization-promoting outer layer for hot strength, made from chlorinated metallurgical silicon instead of mined quartz.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: removes the Spruce Pine dependency for wafer supply using Si, O, Cl, H only; U.S. fiber makers already run the process.

title: Gas-storage MOF chemistry: zinc-imidazolate vapor-deposited photoresist
idea: Borrow zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIF-8) from gas separation: grow the resist by vapor-phase conversion of an ALD ZnO film into ZIF-8 (Zn, C, H, N), which decomposes under EUV, DUV or e-beam and develops in vapor, replacing Sn-, Hf- or Zr-based metal-oxide EUV resists and spin tracks.
why: EUV throughput (fact 4): Zn absorbs EUV far better than organic resists, so lower dose and more wafers per scanner-hour; solvent-free conformal coating; no Hf.

title: DNA nanotechnology: origami placement templates for cell contacts
idea: Borrow from biotech: DUV-pattern only coarse binding sites, let DNA origami tiles (C, H, N, O, P) dock into them by shape-selective placement, each carrying a designed 3-5 nm contact or landing-pad pattern, then transfer it into SiO2 by DNA-mediated vapor HF etching.
why: EUV dependence (fact 4): the finest array features come from molecular self-assembly on a DUV grid; DNA synthesis cost has fallen ~10^6x; zero banned elements.

title: Float-glass online APCVD: vacuum-free mold and interlayer oxides
idea: Float-glass lines coat moving ribbons at atmospheric pressure with SiO2 and SiOxCy; adapt gas-curtain-isolated atmospheric CVD heads (TEOS/ozone, silane/N2O) for DRAM's thick capacitor mold oxides, interlayer dielectrics and gap fills, with no vacuum chamber, load lock or turbo pump.
why: Tool capex and energy (fact 4): APCVD is ~1/3 the cost and footprint of PECVD per wafer-hour, and 1-2 um mold stacks are a heavy deposition load; Si, O, N, C, H only.

title: Hydrogen-cooled power generators: helium-free wafer chuck cooling
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because its thermal conductivity beats helium's; replace helium backside gas in etch, deposition and implant electrostatic chucks with low-pressure H2 or forming gas from on-site electrolysis, using the generator industry's purity monitoring and leak detection.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline; He is not Earth-abundant in practice): H2 ~0.18 W/m-K versus He ~0.15 keeps high-AR etch running through a helium crisis.

title: Stainless-steel self-passivation: copper-manganese self-forming barriers
idea: Stainless steel protects itself as chromium segregates into a thin oxide; use a Cu-Mn alloy seed so on anneal Mn migrates to the dielectric and forms a ~2 nm MnSixOy barrier, eliminating the TaN/Ta barrier PVD steps in DRAM copper wiring.
why: Ta-free (constraint) with fewer steps (fact 4): removes 2 PVD steps per metal level and frees 3-5 nm of line width for copper, lowering periphery RC (fact 7).

title: Automotive microcontroller fabs: hafnium-free poly-SiON periphery wafers
idea: Carmakers' MCUs run on 40/28 nm poly-gate SiON processes in underused U.S. fabs; move row decoders, wordline drivers, I/O and control onto such a Hf-free wafer (contacts in TiN-lined Al, not W) and hybrid-bond it to the array wafer, which keeps only pitch-matched sense amps.
why: Hf-free, EUV-free periphery (facts 4, 7): much of the ~49% periphery leaves the costly array wafer, cutting array-wafer area per bit ~30-40% and putting idle U.S. mature capacity to work.

title: Display-industry sputtered zinc oxynitride channels for back-end gain-cell tiers
idea: The display industry sputters large-area oxide TFT channels; with In and Ga banned, use reactive-sputtered zinc oxynitride (ZnON, mobility ~50-100 cm2/Vs) with Al2O3/SiO2 gates to stack 2T0C gain-cell tiers above CMOS, each tier made by room-temperature sputtering and DUV litho, no epitaxy.
why: 3D DRAM manufacturability (fact 2) and capex (fact 4): tiers come from cheap PVD tools; Zn, O, N, Al are abundant. Risk: ZnON stability and leakage tail.

title: LTPS laser crystallization with argon-fluoride light for silicon-only tiers
idea: Borrow the phone-display LTPS line: deposit amorphous Si per tier and melt-crystallize it with a line-beam excimer laser using sequential lateral solidification for cell-sized grains; use ArF instead of the usual XeCl so even the laser gas is abundant, and the heat stays in the top ~50 nm so dozens of tiers stack without disturbing lower ones.
why: 3D DRAM (fact 2) with only Si: no In/Ga oxide semiconductors and no SiGe epitaxy; Gen-8-proven annealers; tier cost is about one deposition plus one anneal.

title: Jewelry lost-wax: sacrificial zinc-oxide layers for lateral 3D cavities
idea: Lost-wax casting relies on a filler that is easy to remove; build the 3D DRAM tier stack with sputtered ZnO sacrificial layers between Si or SiN tiers, then dissolve the ZnO in dilute acetic acid, which leaves Si, SiO2 and SiN untouched, carving micron-deep lateral capacitor cavities from one vertical slit.
why: 3D capacitor blocker (fact 2): replaces SiGe epitaxy and aggressive vapor etch with sputtering and a mild wet etch, cutting epi tool needs and recess variability; Zn and O are abundant.

title: Razor-blade coatings: tetrahedral amorphous carbon deep-etch hardmasks
idea: Razor blades and engine parts are coated with ta-C (>70% sp3 diamond-like carbon) by filtered cathodic arc; use 100-200 nm boron-optional ta-C as the hardmask for capacitor and contact deep etch in place of thick amorphous-carbon and tungsten-doped carbon hardmasks.
why: Etch capital (facts 1, 4): ~2-3x the selectivity of a-C, so a thinner mask, lower total AR and ~20-30% shorter etch; C and B only, no W.

title: Wireless charging coils: TSV-free inductively stacked HBM
idea: Borrow Qi chargers and RFID near-field links: stack thinned DRAM dies without TSVs, pass data through on-chip aluminum spiral coils across ~10 um adhesive layers at Gb/s per coil, and bring power through a few wide edge or through-mold vias.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6: ~3x area per bit, -20-30% yield): removes TSV etch, Cu fill with Ta barriers and keep-out zones, moving stacked memory back toward DDR5 area efficiency.

title: Green-building LEED rating applied to memory supply chains
idea: LEED made builders compete on green features; create a 'chokepoint-free memory' rating that scores DRAM by banned-element content (Hf, Ru, Co, W, Ta, In, Ga), helium use and quartz source, and tie federal and hyperscaler purchase preference and accelerated depreciation to higher grades.
why: Policy for capital and resilience: a premium market repays R&D on abundant-element processes and shields U.S. fabs from W and Ga export controls.
